summary: Round-4 verify, narrow scope. Every fix to my round-3 findings holds, and the three measurable claims in the delta that I could reach were measured in my own tree: (1) the raised rate floor kills multipliedBy(2) -- the mutant lands at exactly 3 against isBetween(4L,30L), while the honest run measured 7 three times at load average 186, so the floor keeps 1.75x slack; (2) the close() comment's masking claim is exact -- dropping renewer.interrupt() alone is green, dropping the post-tick closed check alone is green, dropping BOTH fails aCallerAfterCLOSEIsToldCLOSEDRatherThanFENCED in 0.038s with 'lost its lease ... fenced'; (3) M4.40's 'the reversed order is green today, measured' holds -- leases.release() before renewer.interrupt() leaves the whole sequencer module at 246 tests, 0 failures. The close() comment's null-belief claim is also true by reading: releaseLocked() sets belief=null and renewLocked() returns at 'mine == null' before any store call, so the interrupt saves no request. No request rate is touched: the renewer is one conditional PUT per interval per node. Two minors, both of the claim-truth class this task keeps producing, both landing under minors-land.

findings.title: The delta's new 'measured' clause names the wrong assertion as the fence-on-IOException detector
findings.detail: The added clause says the fence-on-IOException mutation 'still dies, but at awaitExpiryPast's twenty-second deadline instead of at the `commit` two lines below'. On the staged tree it dies at neither. Measured in the reviewer tree with --rerun-tasks, counts read from TEST-binjava.sequencer.LocalSequencerRenewTest.xml: replacing the IOException catch body with 'fenced = true; return;' fails aStoreFAILUREDuringRenewDoesNotFenceAHealthyLeader at tickAndAwaitProcessed's own assertion, '[the renewer processed the tick and came back round] Expecting value to be true but was false', after 5.04s -- because fencing terminates the renewer so it never releases `parked` again. The commit two lines below never runs. Removing `parked.drainPermits()` as well changes nothing: same assertion, 5.08s. That is because the stale-permit premise is unreachable as staged -- tickAndAwaitProcessed is called exactly once (:291) and no ticker.tick() precedes it in that test (:301 is after), so the drain can only ever drain zero permits. The drain is fine as defence; the sentence explaining what it buys is not what the tree does.
findings.failure_scenario: A later session trusts the comment, believes the seq.commit(...) line is what catches a fence-on-IOException regression, and relaxes or removes the 5s rendezvous assertion (for instance replacing it with a poll that tolerates a dead renewer) as redundant synchronisation. The rendezvous was in fact the only assertion that fires under that mutation, so the regression -- every store hiccup fencing the leader, the cluster-wide failover this task exists to remove -- then lands green or is caught 20s later by an assertion whose message names renewal, not fencing.

findings.title: The mechanism struck from baselines/review.txt in this same delta survives verbatim in the test file, contradicting the same file 25 lines above
findings.detail: The delta corrects the cap argument to 'THE WINDOW IS BEFORE THE SEAL LANDS, not after: once a successor has sealed, CommitLog already refuses'. The identical pre-correction claim is still at :235-237 -- 'A tick that renewed and IGNORED the answer would be worse than no tick: the old leader keeps committing into a chain a successor has already sealed, reassigning offsets it has issued. I2.' CommitLog does refuse: sealedAt is checked at CommitLog.java:284 and a slot lost to a SEAL throws fenced() at :338, and slots are consecutive so a fenced leader cannot write past the seal. The same file says so at :208-212 ('CommitLog already refuses to write into a sealed chain with exactly that word'), which is why the first draft of the fenced test passed against a renewer-less tree. Separately, 'worse than no tick' -- which baselines/review.txt:17 still carries as 'ships something strictly WORSE than no tick' -- is not supported in either place: with no tick the holder is equally ignorant and commits in exactly the same acquire-to-seal window, and a working tick makes that window rarer because the lease stops lapsing. The honest statement is 'no better than no tick, while shipping a renewer that ignores a signal its own contract calls mandatory', which still carries the do-not-split conclusion. This is one copy of a fact fixed and its duplicate missed, which is the failure mode backlog-done.md already records against M4.0.
findings.failure_scenario: A session planning M4.39 or the M5 supervisor tick reads :235-237, concludes the seal is not a barrier for a fenced leader, and either re-adds a seal check CommitLog already has or -- worse -- weighs the fence's cost against a phantom I2 that the seal protocol already closes, distorting the ADR-0027 successor's quantity that M4.39 exists to state.
